skill.name: skill-rails-upgrade
skill.description: Assess Ruby on Rails applications for version upgrades, dependency updates, and selective configuration merges.
skill.summary: Plan Rails upgrades with version checks, official guidance, dependency review, and cautious file merge steps.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives, including filenames, URLs, package names, and code fences. Several real command examples can modify dependencies, files, credentials, or database state, so they should require explicit user approval. No evidence of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Project-mutating commands are included in the upgrade workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running dependency updates, Rails generators, migrations, server starts, or console commands.

remediation.issue: Network lookups depend on public external services.
remediation.suggestion: Limit network requests to public Rails, GitHub, railsdiff, and npm metadata, and avoid sending private project files to those services.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples can be mistaken for executable backtick patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Label read-only checks, approval-required commands, and manual examples clearly so scanners and users can distinguish their intent.

static_findings.snippet: 1. First, check `Gemfile.lock` for the exact installed version (look for `rails (x.y.z)`)
2. If not found, check `Gemfile` for the version constraint
This returns the latest stable version tag (e.g., `v8.0.1`). Strip the 'v' prefix for comparison.
If `package.json` exists, check for these Rails-related packages:
| `@hotwired/turbo-rails` | Turbo Drive/Frames/Streams | Should match Rails version era |
| `@hotwired/stimulus` | Stimulus JS framework | Generally stable across Rails versions |
| `@rails/actioncable` | WebSocket support | Should match Rails version |
| `@rails/activestorage` | Direct uploads | Should match Rails version |
| `@rails/actiontext` | Rich text editing | Should match Rails version |
| `@rails/request.js` | Rails UJS replacement | Should match Rails version era |
If the app uses importmap-rails, check `config/importmap.rb` for pinned versions:
- Run `npm update @rails/actioncable @rails/activestorage` to match Rails version
6. **DO NOT run `rails app:update` directly** - use the selective merge process below
**IMPORTANT:** Do NOT run `rails app:update` as it overwrites files without considering local custom
| **Unchanged locally** | Safe to overwrite | `public/404.html` (if not customized) |
3. Once all defaults are enabled and tested, update `config/application.rb`:
- If `gh` CLI is not authenticated, instruct the user to run `gh auth login`

content.value_statement: Rails upgrades can hide breaking changes, dependency drift, and risky file overwrites. This skill builds a structured upgrade assessment and selective merge plan before changes are applied.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the current project has the core files expected in a Rails application.
Finds the installed Rails version from Gemfile.lock or the Gemfile version constraint.
Compares the current version with recent Rails releases from GitHub.
Uses the Rails upgrade guide and railsdiff references to summarize relevant changes.
Reviews Rails-related JavaScript packages for npm, yarn, and importmap projects.
Creates a selective file merge plan that separates new files, safe updates, and manual merges.
limitations: Requires project access and may need network access for GitHub, Rails guides, railsdiff, or npm metadata.
Cannot prove upgrade compatibility without running the application test suite.
railsdiff may not provide every exact source and target version pair.
Generated merge plans still need human review before files or databases are changed.

use_cases.title: Plan a Major Rails Upgrade
use_cases.description: Map version changes, likely breaking changes, and configuration updates before moving to a new Rails major version.

use_cases.title: Estimate Client Upgrade Scope
use_cases.description: Produce a concise assessment of dependency work, file merge risk, and test expectations for a Rails upgrade proposal.

use_cases.title: Review Sprint Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify upgrade blockers, local customizations, and verification steps before committing team time to framework maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Current Version
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment for a Rails project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Rails app. Tell me the current Rails version, latest stable version, upgrade type, and first risks to review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Target Upgrade
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a known target release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess the upgrade from my current Rails version to the target version I provide. Include guide changes, railsdiff changes, and JavaScript dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Merge Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my local config, bin, and public files with Rails default changes. Separate new files, safe updates, manual merges, and skipped changes.

prompt_templates.title: Execute Approved Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: After I approve the upgrade plan, apply only the agreed changes. Then run migrations, run tests, and summarize failures and follow-up work.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for an upgrade check from Rails 7.1 to Rails 8.0.
output: Complexity: Large because the upgrade crosses a major version.
Next actions: review deprecations, compare default files, update dependencies on a clean branch, and run tests.

output_examples.input: A project has a customized application configuration file and a changed bin script.
output: Manual merge needed for application configuration because local settings must be preserved.
Manual merge needed for the bin script because the project uses custom process management.
Safe updates can proceed only for files that match Rails defaults.

output_examples.input: A Rails app uses importmap and Hotwire packages.
output: Package manager: importmap with Rails-related pins.
Review Turbo and Stimulus pins against the target Rails release.
Apply pin updates only after confirming the framework upgrade path.

best_practices: Start from a clean branch with the current test suite passing.
Review deprecation warnings before changing the Rails version.
Confirm every generated file update before overwriting local customizations.
anti_patterns: Running a full Rails app update without checking local changes first.
Treating JavaScript and importmap dependencies as unrelated to the Rails upgrade.
Starting a major upgrade without a rollback plan and test baseline.

faq.question: Does this skill upgrade the app automatically?
faq.answer: It focuses on assessment and planning first. It should apply changes only after the user approves a specific plan.

faq.question: Can it handle major Rails upgrades?
faq.answer: Yes. It classifies major upgrades as higher complexity and highlights breaking changes, dependency work, and manual merge needs.

faq.question: Does it check JavaScript dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks common Hotwire and Rails JavaScript packages for npm, yarn, and importmap-based applications.

faq.question: What happens if railsdiff lacks an exact comparison?
faq.answer: The skill should try nearby major and minor version comparisons, then clearly state the limitation.

faq.question: Is a passing test suite still required?
faq.answer: Yes. The assessment can guide the work, but tests are required to validate compatibility.

faq.question: Will it preserve local configuration changes?
faq.answer: It is designed to detect local customizations and separate them into manual merge items before changes are made.
